subject: Execution sequencing & emergency rollback questionnaire — Zenith Bank RFP
messages:
From: Priya Shah <priya.shah@zenithbank.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Tom Ellis <t.ellis@zenithbank.com>
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Zenith RFP: execution sequencing & rollback Qs

Hi Jonas —

Thanks for the initial response and the architecture diagram yesterday. Procurement has a few follow-ups specifically focused on execution sequence and rollback controls for our production cutover. We need this detail in the RFP appendix so internal risk and DB teams can sign off. Can you please provide the following by EOD Friday?

1) A step-by-step execution sequence for a phased go-live (pilot -> canary -> full traffic) including the owners for each step.
2) Explicit rollback criteria at each stage (pilot failure, canary health degradation, post-cutover anomalies).
3) Expected business-impact windows (e.g., acceptable error rates, latency SLO deviations) that trigger immediate rollback.
4) Suggested monitoring/alerting hooks and the health metrics you will expose to our SRE team.
5) Any constraints around DB schema migrations or data sync windows.

We also need to see an example of a 48-hour canary runbook and any stop-the-line run triggers. We're collecting vendor responses into a spreadsheet (attached) — please return a filled copy if possible.

Thanks — Priya
Priya Shah
VP, Vendor Risk & Procurement
Zenith Bank

[Attachment: zenith_requested_timeline.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)]

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priya Shah <priya.shah@zenithbank.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Zenith RFP: execution sequencing & rollback Qs

Priya —

Appreciate the clarity. Attached is a concise execution sequence doc and a preliminary filled copy of your spreadsheet. High level answers below; we'll expand into the appendix doc and deliver a 48-hour canary runbook by Friday EOD.

Quick summary:
- Pilot (week 1): single service path + internal users, controlled traffic <1% via header routing. Owner: Marissa (onboarding PM). Decision gate: correctness on key prompt sets, no P0 errors for 24h.
- Canary (48 hours): 1-5% traffic, split across regions; health checks every 1 min. Owner: Laura (Ops lead). Decision gate: sustained SLA compliance (latency p95 < 400ms, error rate <0.5%) and quality checks against golden prompts.
- Gradual ramp (next 7 days): ramp to 25/50/100% with automated automated rollback thresholds. Owner: Jonas.

Rollback criteria (examples):
- Pilot: any data-corruption or KV cache invalidation requires immediate stop and rollback to previous model version.
- Canary: if p95 latency breaches 2x baseline for 5 consecutive minutes OR error rate >1% for 10 minutes -> pause and revert canary routing.
- Post-cutover: if quality regressions (measured via eval set) exceed 3 percentage points vs baseline -> automatic staged rollback to last verified model.

Monitoring hooks:
- Expose per-route p50/p95/p99 latency, per-route 1min error rate, token consumption, model version tagging, and per-request hashes to correlate with your logs. We'll provide a Grafana dashboard + Alertmanager rules (Slack + PagerDuty).

DB constraints: Redwood does not write to your primary transactional DB for inference workflows — we recommend a read-only sync plus a short-lived write queue for closures (optional). If you require model-side caching of user metadata, we advise a pre-cutover schema freeze for 48 hours. Any migrations that touch request routing tables must be completed outside the canary window or coordinated with an explicit migration step we own.

Deliverables attached: redwood_execution_sequence_v1.pdf (execution sequence + triggers) and filled zenith spreadsheet. We'll follow up with the full 48-hour canary runbook.

Next step: Laura and Marissa will join a call on Friday at 10am PT to walk the runbook. Can you confirm?

—Jonas
Jonas Weber
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference

[Attachments: redwood_execution_sequence_v1.pdf (application/pdf), zenith_requested_timeline_filled.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)]

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 13 May 2027 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: Zenith RFP — canary thresholds and DB notes

Team —

Looping you in before Friday's call. Priya asked for explicit stop-the-line criteria and ownership. A few items I want aligned before we present:

1) Canary health aggregator: Laura, can you confirm the exact alert rule names you'll push to their PagerDuty? I proposed: "zenith_canary_latency_breach", "zenith_canary_error_rate_spike", "zenith_quality_regression".
2) DB freeze: We must request a 48h schema freeze prior to pilot. Aditya, what is the minimum lead time we need for our engineers to validate the read-only sync?
3) Rollback automation: Marissa — do we want to use our automated model-variant rollback (auto-revert after N failures) or a manual switch with runbook steps? Manual gives more control but increases MTTR. I'm inclined to recommend auto-revert for canary, manual for post-cutover.

Please reply inline with short bullets so I can update the appendix. Also flag any constraints we should not promise.

Thanks — Jonas

From: Priya Shah <priya.shah@zenithbank.com>

Cc: Tom Ellis <t.ellis@zenithbank.com>, CloudOps Integrations <ops@cloudops.io>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 14:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Execution sequencing & emergency rollback questionnaire — Zenith Bank RFP

Jonas —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the attachments. Confirm Friday 10am PT works for the walkthrough — I'll invite Tom (SRE) and our migration lead. A couple of clarifying asks ahead of the call:

- For canary automation, we prefer a "manual-confirmed rollback" for any change that affects traffic routing in our production CIDR. We can accept automated reversion for model-parameter-only changes, but traffic-routing reversion requires on-call approval.
- For DB schema freeze: 72 hours minimum before pilot start. We need a signed attestation that Redwood will not attempt any writes to primary transactional systems outside the agreed write queue.
- For the 48-hour canary runbook, can you include a pre-flight checklist with exact synthetic prompt sets we'll run and an acceptance script we can execute?

We'll upload a pre-approved Drafter NDA/Attestation and the signed migration constraints doc during the call.

Priya

Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 16:22:00 -0700
Subject: Final: Zenith RFP — execution appendix, 48h canary runbook & attestation

Priya / Tom —

Appended is the finalized execution appendix and a 48-hour canary runbook that incorporates your constraints: manual-confirmed routing rollbacks, 72-hour schema freeze, and a pre-flight acceptance script with synthetic prompts. Key items below:

- Owners: Pilot (Marissa), Canary (Laura), Ramp/Final (Jonas). Contact cards are in the runbook.
- Canary acceptance script: 6 golden prompts (attached) executed every 2 hours; pass requires semantic fidelity score >0.82 and p95 latency <400ms.
- Stop-the-line triggers: manual confirmation required to revert routing changes OR automatic model-variant revert for tokenization/regression anomalies.
- Rollback procedure: API-driven variant re-routing (automated) + a mandatory post-rollback incident review within 4 business hours.
- Data handling attestation: Redwood confirms no direct writes to Zenith primary transactional DB outside the agreed write queue. We'll countersign the migration constraints doc on the call.

Attachments included: redwood_execution_sequence_v1.pdf (final), zenith_canary_runbook_48h.pdf, golden_prompt_set.txt, zenith_requested_timeline_filled.xlsx. DocuSign for the migration constraints envelope has been sent: https://docusign.com/XYZ-Envelope-12345

Next steps:
1) Call Friday 10am PT — agenda: runbook walk, sign attestation, finalize on-call rotations.
2) We'll produce a short runbook rehearsal playbook for your SREs to execute one week before pilot.

If any of the technical acceptance thresholds are blockers, flag them now and we'll adjust the appendix.

Cheers — Jonas
Jonas Weber
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference
